daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo attended the Independence Day carnival at the National Monument on the evening of 17 August, sitting alongside Vice President Gibran at the public celebration. The PKS Secretary General said the Electoral Bill should be passed as soon as possible. DPR Chairwoman Puan Maharani expressed condolences to NTT earthquake victims and emphasized social justice, while the DPR as an institution coordinated assistance and evacuation for those affected by the disaster.

  • DPD Chair stated that national unity must be maintained.
  • The Presidential Palace defended President Prabowo's Independence Day speech amid controversy over remarks about onion peeler wages, urging focus on the speech's substance.
  • The Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal and Security Affairs said the red-and-white flag and Garuda Pancasila must be honored.
  • BEM UI announced it will hold a demonstration at Bundaran HI on 18 August.
  • The Minister of Cooperatives said a cooperative building being used as a badminton court is acceptable temporarily, pending a presidential regulation.
  • Kompas reported on regional governments beginning to resist central authority.

Foreign Policy & Defence

French-made Rafale fighter jets and A400M transport aircraft conducted their debut flypast over Merdeka Palace during Indonesia's 81st Independence Day ceremony on 17 August. King Salman and the Saudi Crown Prince congratulated President Prabowo on Indonesia's Independence Day and prayed for NTT earthquake victims. Russian President Putin also sent Independence Day greetings to President Prabowo, while the US Secretary of State congratulated Indonesia on its 81st anniversary.

  • Australia highlighted Indonesia's role in maintaining regional security.
  • Indonesia and seven other nations accused Israel of obstructing the Gaza peace roadmap.
  • The TNI declared Hitadipa village in Intan Jaya a "peaceful village" on Independence Day.
  • One TNI soldier was killed and two wounded in a firefight with OPM during Independence Day celebrations in Mimika.
  • The military deployed 10 units of defense equipment to Labuan Bajo and Maumere in NTT to accelerate logistics distribution.

Other

The government has confirmed 68 people dead and 213 injured following the magnitude 7.7 earthquake that struck East Nusa Tenggara, with 1,624 aftershocks recorded, the largest measuring 6.2. The Home Affairs Minister outlined priority recovery plans based on data-driven approaches and distributed financial assistance to families of earthquake victims. The government has allocated Rp 5 trillion for emergency response, while the Health Ministry dispatched two field hospitals to NTT.

  • A minister said 86 percent of base transceiver stations have been restored in NTT after the earthquake.
  • The government announced it will economically enfranchise citizens, according to a minister.
  • Indonesia's Rp 5 million e-motorcycle incentive awaits finance ministry regulation.
  • Indonesia is pushing three priority agendas to strengthen digital sovereignty.
  • Bali authorities granted Independence Day remissions resulting in four foreign inmates being freed.
